heard: An asteroid zipped 1,830 miles above Earth, yet nobody saw it coming. In August 2020, this SUV-sized space rock approached from the hidden, blinding direction of the bright sun. Traveling at a blistering 27,600 miles per hour, it remained entirely invisible to all our ground-based observatories. Earth's massive gravity then violently bent the trajectory of this rock by roughly 45 degrees of arc. The Zwicky transient facility finally spotted the tiny object six hours after its closest, most terrifying approach. This event remains the absolute closest non-impacting asteroid flyby ever recorded by our modern global science. The massive blind spot created by the sun is why we never saw that asteroid.
